article.title: The word for "the": ha- and the doubled letter
article.summary: Hebrew has one word for "the", a small prefix glued to the front of a noun.

drill.explain: the earth = ha- + no dagesh: the first letter cannot take one; base word אֲדָמָה
the strait = ha- + doubled first letter (dagesh); base word מֵצַר
the body = ha- + doubled first letter (dagesh); base word גּוּף

prefixes.title: One-letter prefixes: ve-, be-, le-, me-, she-
prefixes.summary: Small words such as and, in, to, from and that are written as one letter stuck to the next word.

construct.title: Construct state: the "of" chain
construct.summary: Two nouns side by side can mean "X of Y" without a separate word for of.

drill.prompt: Which chain means "king of the world"?
drill.explain: king of the world: two nouns side by side, in the line "Blessing formula (Baruch atah Adonai Eloheinu Melech ha'olam)"

drill.prompt: Which chain means "lights of the fire"?
drill.explain: lights of the fire: two nouns side by side, in the line "Havdalah: blessing over the flame"

drill.prompt: Which chain means "name of the glory of his kingship"?
drill.explain: name of the glory of his kingship: two nouns side by side, in the line "Baruch shem (said after Shema line)"

plurals.title: Plural patterns: -im and -ot
plurals.summary: Most masculine nouns take -im and most feminine nouns take -ot, with exceptions.

drill.explain: יוֹם (masculine, day) -> יָמִים: the usual ending
שָׁנָה (feminine, year) -> שָׁנִים: an exception to the usual ending
בֵּן (masculine, son) -> בָּנִים: the usual ending

roots.title: The three-letter root
roots.summary: Many Hebrew words are built on a skeleton of usually three consonants that carries a core meaning.

drill.prompt: Which word is listed under the same family letters א־נ־שׁ as אָנוּשׁ ("mortal")?
drill.explain: אָנוּשׁ and נָשִׁים are both listed under the letters א־נ־שׁ in the word list. A Hebrew reader has not yet confirmed them as one root.

drill.prompt: Which word is listed under the same family letters פ־נ־ה as פָּנִים ("face")?
drill.explain: פָּנִים and פָּנָה are both listed under the letters פ־נ־ה in the word list. A Hebrew reader has not yet confirmed them as one root.

drill.prompt: Which word is listed under the same family letters מ־צ־א as מָצוּי ("regular")?
drill.explain: מָצוּי and מָצָא are both listed under the letters מ־צ־א in the word list. A Hebrew reader has not yet confirmed them as one root.
